transcript.content: Hello, welcome. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. I came in because... well, my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I could do in my sleep before—and the numbers and words just scatter on me. I just can't seem to think straight.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, energy level, or interest in daily activities along with these memory and thinking problems?

Yes, my mood has definitely changed. Most days, I wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It just sits there. And it's hard to explain, but even when my wife is talking kindly to me, just going about her day, I feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well. I just can't seem to reach out of it.
Have you noticed that you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or spending time with family?

Yes, I have. I just... I haven't touched the wood pieces sitting out on my workbench. I've been skipping out on choir planning, and chess too. Even fishing... it just sounds like more effort than it's worth right now. And that's really not like me at all.
Have you noticed any worsening in your ability to remember things, follow conversations, or handle daily tasks like managing money or following a recipe?

I don't think it's any worse than what I mentioned when we first sat down. I mean, my wife handles most of the bills, and I haven't really tried to cook or follow any recipes lately, so I haven't noticed anything there. As for conversations... I can follow what people are saying just fine. I just don't really have the energy to join in much.

Have you had any trouble keeping track of the date, knowing where you are, or figuring out the right thing to do in common situations—like if something unexpected happened while driving or while talking with someone?

No, I haven't noticed any trouble with that. I know what day it is, and I always know where I am. I haven't really been driving much lately, just because I don't have the motivation to go anywhere, but I haven't had any issues figuring out what to do if something comes up. I just feel... drained, not confused about where I am or what's going on.
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or increased fatigue, even when doing simple tasks?

No, not really. I know I just said a minute ago that I feel drained, but... it's not really a physical exhaustion. Doing simple things around the house doesn't wear me out or anything. I just... I don't have the drive to do them in the first place. But physically, my energy for basic tasks is fine. I haven't noticed any real fatigue like that.
Have you found it harder to think clearly or make decisions lately, even about small things?

Yes, actually. That's a big part of why I came in today. My mind just... it will not hold onto things anymore. I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program, which is something I could do in my sleep before, and the numbers and words just scatter on me. It's like I can't keep my thoughts straight to even do the small things.
Have you noticed these problems with your thinking—like the difficulty keeping your thoughts straight—before your mood started to change, or did they begin around the same time as the mood changes?

I'm... I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to pin down an exact timeline. I don't know if my mind started getting scattered before I started feeling so down, or if they both kind of hit me at the same time. It just feels like it's all rolled into one big mess lately, so I really couldn't tell you which came first.
Have you ever experienced a time in the past when you felt this down or had this much trouble thinking clearly, or is this the first time you've had symptoms like these?
No, I don't think so. I've never really felt like this before... not this down, and definitely not this foggy in my head. This is all pretty new to me, to be honest.

Over the past two weeks, have you experienced any of the following nearly every day: little interest or pleasure in doing things, feeling down or hopeless, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, feeling tired or having no energy, poor appetite or overeating, feeling worthless or guilty, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of being better off dead or hurting yourself?

That's, uh, a lot of things at once. Well, like I mentioned, feeling down and having trouble concentrating... yes, that's been pretty much every day. But as for the rest of that list you just read off... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed any changes with my sleep or my appetite or the other stuff. I just know the sadness and the foggy head are there constantly, and that's what's really bothering me.
Have you had any thoughts of being better off dead or hurting yourself in any way?

Yes, I have. I keep thinking that my family might just be better off without me around. And... well, when I'm out near my workshop, I actually get a little scared of where my thoughts could go if I were left alone out there.
Have you ever had a period of time when your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt extremely energetic or overly confident, even for a few days?

No, I can't say that I have. I've never really had a time where I felt unusually high or energetic like that. I've always been a pretty steady guy... well, at least until lately with all this sadness. But no, I've never had any bursts of energy or felt overly confident.
Do you feel that your difficulty concentrating and your memory problems happen mostly when you're feeling down, or do they also happen when your mood is better?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. Honestly, I haven't had a time where my mood was better lately to even compare it to. It just feels like the sadness and the foggy head are always there together. So, I don't really know if the concentration issues would happen if I felt okay, because... well, I just haven't felt okay in a while.

Can you think back to times in your life when you were not feeling down—like maybe a year ago or before this sadness started—were you still having trouble concentrating or keeping your thoughts straight back then?

No, not at all. Back then, my mind was sharp. I could read a book, work on a project in the shop, keep track of whatever I needed to do without any issue. The trouble focusing... the memory slipping... that's all new. It really just started when this whole heavy cloud settled over me. Before that, I didn't have any problems keeping my thoughts straight.

Can you think of a time recently, even briefly, when your mood felt a little better—like maybe after talking with a friend or seeing a grandchild—when you noticed if your thinking or concentration also improved along with your mood?

I... I honestly don't know. Like I said, there really haven't been any times where I felt better lately. Even if I see my grandkids, which I love, the sadness is just... it's still there. It doesn't lift. So I haven't had a chance to see if my concentration would get better, because the mood just hasn't improved at all.
Can you recall if there were any instances, even brief ones, when your mood was slightly better and you noticed if your thinking or concentration problems also lessened at all?

I think we're going in circles a bit here, Doc. Like I was just saying... I really can't think of a single instance lately where my mood lifted, even for a minute. It's just a constant heavy feeling every single day. 

So, no, I haven't noticed my thinking clear up, because the mood hasn't cleared up either. I wish I could give you a different answer, but I just don't have those moments of feeling better right now to even compare it to.
Have you noticed that on days when you feel a little less sad, even slightly, your thinking or concentration gets any better at all?

Doc, I... I don't know how else to explain it. You're asking the exact same thing again. Like I just said, I don't have days where I feel less sad. Not even a little bit. Every single day is just as heavy as the last. So I really can't tell you if my concentration improves on better days, because I just don't have any better days right now.
